# Ajitamāṇavapucchā (Snp 5.2 (PTS Snp 197))

**ID:** Snp 5.2 (PTS Snp 197)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Ajitamāṇavapucchā
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Questions of the Student Ajita
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/snp5.2
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ajitamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Ajita") is the second discourse of the *Pārāyanavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* (vv. 1032–1039, PTS Snp 197) [Norman 1997-2001; Hazra 1994; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. In the narrative setting established by the *Vatthugāthā*, Ajita is the first of the sixteen brāhmaṇa mendicant pupils sent by the ascetic Bāvarī to question the Buddha [Goldstone 1978; Hazra 1994; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. Ajita inquires into the nature of the world's affliction, whereupon the Buddha explains that the world is enveloped in ignorance and marred by greed and desire; the Buddha describes mindfulness (*smṛti*) as the dam or protective barrier (*saṃvara*) checking the stream of samsara, and teaches that the cessation of consciousness (*viññāṇa*) brings the complete cessation of name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*) [SuttaCentral; Hazra 1994; Colloque Lamotte 1993; Pande 1974].

The discourse preserves very ancient material with notable parallels across early Indian religious literature. A closely resembling parallel to Ajita's question is transmitted in Jain literature in the *Isibhāsiyāiṁ* 29.1 [SuttaCentral; Colloque Lamotte 1993]. In Sanskrit Buddhist literature, the text is preserved as the *Ajitapraśna*, canonical versions of which are quoted in the *Śarīrārthagāthā* of the *Yogācārabhūmi* and in Central Asian manuscript fragments, containing verses corresponding to the Pali discourse alongside verses from the *Udayamāṇavapucchā* [Norman 1997-2001; Lee 2017; SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. In canonical and post-canonical Pali literature, the discourse is the subject of an early exegetical commentary in the *Ajitamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (*Cūḷaniddesa* 5, as well as Cnd 2), and its verses are cited and expounded in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 5 and Ne 16), the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 1 and Pe 5), and the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12.31) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus; Lamotte, Le Traité; Pande 1974].
